name: Bermuda: self-employed

tests: No personal income tax. Payroll tax applies to remuneration for work in Bermuda, including what a self-employed person takes out of the business.

calendar.note: Payroll tax is filed and paid quarterly, by 15 January, 15 April, 15 July and 15 October for the quarter just ended. The payroll tax year runs from 1 April. There is no VAT or sales tax.

sources.title: Government of Bermuda: Calculating payroll tax, 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027

workdays.note: Not verified whether deadlines here move off weekends and holidays. Kyros shows the last working day on or before the legal date, so paying on it is always in time, and keeps the reserve locked until the next working day after it.

presets.label: Self-employed: payroll tax on what you take out of the business (0.5% while your payroll is under BMD 200,000 a year); no income tax or VAT. Social insurance is a fixed weekly amount: set it aside as a fixed fee

buckets.name: payroll_tax
buckets.label: Payroll tax at the standard rate for an annual payroll under BMD 200,000

items.name: payroll_tax
items.label: Payroll tax 2026-27 at the standard rate of the payroll's band (0.5% under BMD 200,000, 2% to 350,000, 4.75% to 500,000, 7% to 1 million, 9.5% above), charged on the self-employed person's actual remuneration: what they take out of the business. The estimate uses the profit, the most a self-employed person can take out.

items.name: social_insurance
items.label: Social insurance (Contributory Pensions Act): a self-employed person under 65 pays both shares, BMD 75.30 a week since 4 August 2025 (BMD 3,915.60 a year); BMD 37.65 at 65 or over. A fixed amount: Kyros can set it aside as a fixed fee per period.

notes: Bermuda has no personal income tax, no VAT and no sales tax. A self-employed person is deemed to employ himself and pays payroll tax at the standard rate on his actual remuneration, what he takes out of the business for personal use, up to BMD 1 million a year (Payroll Tax Act 1995, s. 3 and 14). Employees of the business add their own payroll tax.

Social insurance is a fixed weekly amount (BMD 75.30 for a self-employed person under 65 since 4 August 2025), counted in the estimate and suggested as a fixed fee per period. Bermudians and their spouses aged 23 or over earning more than BMD 20,000 also pay a mandatory occupational pension (10% of declared earnings, at most BMD 5,000 a year, per the US Social Security Administration's survey); mandatory health insurance is a premium. Neither is included.
The Bermudian dollar is pegged one to one to the US dollar. The government accepts tax payments in USDC since 2019, and is building a Bermuda Digital Dollar on Stellar.
Rule packs are information, not tax advice. The user confirms the percentages; the vault enforces what the user chose.
